facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable for the credit view, with restrictions. The audited FY2026 statements, the Q1 FY2027 interim statements and the debt note allow every debt instrument, the maturity wall, liquidity and the claims outside debt to be set out from the filings. On an analyst basis, total debt principal is 2.58x LTM EBITDA (4.43x at FY2025) and net debt, after unrestricted cash and short-term investments, is 1.46x. Interest cover is 8.80x on cash interest. Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 1,752.9 million of unrestricted cash and short-term investments plus 669 million of stated revolver availability.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The restrictions matter. First, no source reports EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or a covenant ratio, so every EBITDA-based ratio here is an analyst calculation and the covenant definitions are not supplied. Second, the business is in a steep ramp: operating cash flow was negative and free cash flow deeply negative in Q1 FY2027, funded by 803 million of new unsecured borrowing at foreign subsidiaries that sits outside the guarantor group. Third, claims outside reported debt are large: purchase commitments, customer prepayments and a multi-year capacity agreement that the company says may require material further cash. Fourth, the maturity schedule is only as of 2026-06-30. The NVIDIA purchase of shares for aggregate gross proceeds of 2 billion in March 2026 is the main reason FY2026 debt fell before the Q1 FY2027 rise (10-Q Q1 FY2027 page:18). Fifth, restricted cash of 583 million, almost all held by Silicon Carbide LLC for its own use, is excluded from liquidity. Sixth, the three conflicts in the upstream readiness handoff are carried: the Munich gain follows the audited annual report, and period labels in the Q1 FY2027 narrative follow the statements.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The business and transaction picture is usable for the credit view, with limits. Coherent Corp. is a vertically integrated maker of lasers, transceivers and optical and optoelectronic devices, reported in two segments. The Datacenter & Communications segment is the growth engine and the Industrial segment is shrinking through disposals. Ownership is public: no sponsor or controlling holder is named, although the sources do not list beneficial owners, and no dividend recapitalisation, priming or other creditor-adverse action is documented. The material events are the 2 billion NVIDIA share purchase, the conversion of the Series B preferred stock, the 2025 and 2026 disposals, the 2025 amendments to the Credit Agreement and the 2026 foreign credit facilities. facts.text: The second is the debt structure. No new bond was issued; the 5.00% Senior Notes of 990 million date from 2021. These sit outside the guarantor group and are 802,793 thousand in total; the Company and its other subsidiaries are not parties to them. facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: The fundamental credit view is of a company with strong and improving operating economics that is financing a very large capacity build, with the quality of that build to be proven. On the financial side, analyst EBITDA rose to 1,563,235 thousand LTM from 843,476 thousand in FY2025. Total debt to EBITDA fell from 4.43x in FY2025 to 2.29x in FY2026, and is 2.58x at 2026-09-30, with net debt to EBITDA of 1.46x. Cover is 8.80x on cash interest, and liquidity is 2,421.9 million made up of cash and short-term investments of 1,752.9 million and revolver availability of 669 million. The weight on the other side is cash flow. LTM free cash flow was an outflow of 1,833,632 thousand, Q1 FY2027 capital additions were 775,547 thousand, inventories and customer prepayments grew sharply, and the claims outside reported debt are large: purchase commitments of 3.4 billion for fiscal 2027 at 2026-06-30, contract liabilities, a capacity agreement that may need material cash, and operating leases.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The first finding is cash conversion. In Q1 FY2027 operating cash flow was an outflow of 92,681 thousand and capital additions were 775,547 thousand, so free cash flow was an outflow of 868,228 thousand, and the LTM outflow was 1,833,632 thousand. The mechanism is the capacity and inventory build for AI demand: inventories rose by 760,330 thousand in the quarter, partly offset by accounts payable and customer prepayments, with accrued capital spending of 527,734 thousand in payables at 2026-09-30. The credit implication is that liquidity, not EBITDA, is the near-term constraint: 2,421.9 million of liquidity equals about 2.8 quarters of the Q1 FY2027 burn, and EBITDA less capital additions was negative for the LTM period. The company funded the gap with the 2 billion equity raise of March 2026, cash reserves (short-term investments fell from 825,000 thousand to 200,000 thousand) and 802,793 thousand of foreign borrowing. This is a Documentary Fact for the figures and an Analyst Interpretation for the reading (basis T2; F8, F10, F22).

facts.text: The strengths are as follows. First, scale and operating leverage: FY2026 revenue was 7,118,181 thousand, up 22.5 percent, Q1 FY2027 revenue was up 49.9 percent, and Q1 FY2027 gross margin rose 254 basis points on yields, input costs and pricing, to 39.1 percent, so EBITDA is growing faster than debt (basis F21; CP-1 revenue and margin). Second, moderate leverage and strong cover: total debt to EBITDA of 2.58x, net debt to EBITDA of 1.46x and EBITDA to cash interest of 8.80x LTM, though on an analyst EBITDA that includes 8,922 thousand of gain (CP-1 leverage and cover data). Third, liquidity and a distant maturity wall: 2,421.9 million of liquidity, an undrawn revolver, and only 7.916, 34.375 and 93.629 million due in FY2027 to FY2029 as of 2026-06-30. Fourth, supportive governance in documented actions and a 2 billion equity infusion with no debt service (T5; F8, F13, F15). Fifth, vertical integration and a disclosed multi-year supply agreement with a major AI customer (F1, F7); the claim of a leading supplier position is Management Language and is not adopted (F6).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The weaknesses are as follows. First, concentration in one end market and two customers (T1; F3). Second, negative free cash flow and capital intensity, with capital additions of 32.7 percent of Q1 FY2027 revenue (T2; F22). Third, structural subordination from foreign unsecured debt (T3). Fourth, claims outside reported debt that raise cash demands: purchase commitments of 3.4 billion for fiscal 2027 and 8.4 billion thereafter at 2026-06-30, contract liabilities of 333 million, operating lease liabilities of 346,382 thousand, and a capacity agreement with no stated amount (F10; CP-1 claims outside debt). Fifth, refinancing concentration in 2029 to 2031 and about 75.0 percent of principal at variable rates, where the effect of hedges is not in the upstream handoffs. Sixth, operational and trade exposure in Asia-Pacific with an unquantified export inquiry (T4). Seventh, limited visibility: no reported EBITDA, covenant ratio, customer terms or executed financing documents, and three logged conflicts in the latest quarterly report (F32, F33; C1 to C3).

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the cautious reading is that the earnings base is growing fast: analyst EBITDA rose from 843,476 in FY2025 to 1,563,235 on an LTM basis, Q1 FY2027 EBITDA to cash interest was 17.86x, liquidity of 2,421.9 million is above the springing tests, and management states fiscal 2027 growth well above fiscal 2026. If capital additions of 775,547 in Q1 FY2027 are mainly the capacity build that peaks and then converts to EBITDA, free cash flow would recover quickly. What would make that case win: Q2 FY2027 revenue inside the guided 2.55 billion to 2.75 billion range, a lower Q2 capital additions figure than in Q1, and falling inventory growth. Downside chain with observable triggers: a pause in orders from one of the two large customers (first break: revenue and gross margin) lowers EBITDA while capital commitments of 3.4 billion for fiscal 2027 and lease and debt service stay fixed (transmission), then liquidity falls below 2,421.9 million and revolver availability below 669 million (consequence), then the springing test of 250 million plus the Term B or notes principal becomes relevant before 2029 and refinancing of the 2029 to 2031 wall is harder. Triggers to watch: customer order trends, capital additions, inventory and contract liabilities each quarter, revolver availability, and the covenant certificate when obtainable.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Filings and releases through the quarter ended 2026-09-30 are enough to build the financial base, debt picture and business context, with bounded limits. Covenant levels appear only in the annual report; no financing documents are supplied. | Medium | No executed financing documents, no reported covenant ratios and no EBITDA figure are in the pack, so covenant headroom cannot be measured from the sources. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

The effective source set supports the requested work with limitations. The four requested consumers are all assessed as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, none CONDITIONAL and none BLOCKED. The audited annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases cover the periods the context names, in the reporting currency, up to the evidence cutoff, and every source identifies COHERENT CORP. as the registrant or announcing company. The binding limitations are five. First, no credit agreement, amendment or indenture text is in the pack, so covenant definitions, baskets, guarantor lists and security terms rest on filing summaries. Third, two cross-document conflicts are unresolved and are logged below. Fourth, the pro forma growth rates in the releases have no definition or reconciliation in the pack. Fifth, no fidelity review of the text extraction has been done, and tables, charts and images were not inspected beyond their text. None of these blocks a consumer from starting, and each carries forward as a stated limit.

No source is blocked, draft, unsigned or a duplicate of another. The quarterly statements are unaudited. The filed 10-K and 10-Qs control their own facts. The three releases are management claims that must not override the filings. Chunk coverage was located by section for every source; the sections not listed as supporting an item below (risk factors, human capital, properties, controls, certifications) are retained but were not read for this module.

### Entity and perimeter

The registrant and reporting entity is Coherent Corp. and subsidiaries, consolidated (10-Q Q1 FY2027 page:2). The Senior Credit Facilities borrower is Coherent Corp. (page:11). The 5.000% Senior Notes are guaranteed by each domestic subsidiary that guarantees the Senior Credit Facilities (page:13), and the Senior Credit Facilities are secured on substantially all assets of the borrower and the other guarantors (page:11). The pack does not name those guarantors and has no subsidiaries exhibit text, so the guarantor map is an unresolved gap, not a conclusion. The foreign unsecured credit lines are outside that group: neither the Company nor any other subsidiary is a party to or a guarantor of them (page:14). Silicon Carbide LLC is a subsidiary with outside investors that holds restricted cash for its own use (page:20, page:29); whether it is a guarantor or restricted subsidiary is not stated. ### Financial base view

The financial base is usable for the credit view, with restrictions. The audited FY2026 statements, the Q1 FY2027 interim statements and the debt note allow every debt instrument, the maturity wall, liquidity and the claims outside debt to be set out from the filings. On an analyst basis, total debt principal is 2.58x LTM EBITDA (4.43x at FY2025) and net debt, after unrestricted cash and short-term investments, is 1.46x. Interest cover is 8.80x on cash interest. Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 1,752.9 million of unrestricted cash and short-term investments plus 669 million of stated revolver availability.

The restrictions matter. First, no source reports EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or a covenant ratio, so every EBITDA-based ratio here is an analyst calculation and the covenant definitions are not supplied. Second, the business is in a steep ramp: operating cash flow was negative and free cash flow deeply negative in Q1 FY2027, funded by 803 million of new unsecured borrowing at foreign subsidiaries that sits outside the guarantor group. Third, claims outside reported debt are large: purchase commitments, customer prepayments and a multi-year capacity agreement that the company says may require material further cash. Fourth, the maturity schedule is only as of 2026-06-30. The NVIDIA purchase of shares for aggregate gross proceeds of 2 billion in March 2026 is the main reason FY2026 debt fell before the Q1 FY2027 rise (10-Q Q1 FY2027 page:18). Fifth, restricted cash of 583 million, almost all held by Silicon Carbide LLC for its own use, is excluded from liquidity. Sixth, the three conflicts in the upstream readiness handoff are carried: the Munich gain follows the audited annual report, and period labels in the Q1 FY2027 narrative follow the statements.

### Operating income and EBITDA

Operating income = revenues less cost of goods sold, research and development, selling, general and administrative, restructuring and impairment, plus gain on sale of business. It equals earnings before income taxes plus interest expense less other income, net.
| Period | Calculation | Result | Tie-out |
EBITDA (analyst) = operating income + depreciation + amortization. Depreciation and amortization come from the cash flow statements.
| Period | Calculation | Result |

Depreciation plus amortization LTM = (241,561 + 280,334) + (77,665 + 69,451) − (52,983 + 69,446) = 546,582. This EBITDA does not add back share-based compensation, restructuring, impairment, integration costs or the gain, and it excludes other income, net. The gain on sale of business is inside operating income here, so FY2026 EBITDA includes 124,133 thousand of gain; excluding it, FY2026 EBITDA would be 1,295,623 thousand (1,419,756 − 124,133) and total debt to EBITDA 2.51x (3,257,482 / 1,295,623). LTM EBITDA includes 8,922 thousand of gain (124,133 − 115,211, because Q1 FY2026 is subtracted). Restructuring of 63,390 thousand and impairment of 64,404 thousand in FY2026 are deducted in this measure.
### Adjusted EBITDA (US$m)

Adjusted EBITDA = company non-GAAP operating income (EX-99.1) + depreciation. Non-GAAP operating income already adds back amortization of acquired intangibles, share-based compensation, restructuring, impairment, integration costs and the gain, as the company reconciles them (EX-99.1 2026-08-12 page:8; 2026-11-04 page:8). The FY2025 column was recast by the company to its current non-GAAP method.

### Business and transaction view

The business and transaction picture is usable for the credit view, with limits. Coherent Corp. is a vertically integrated maker of lasers, transceivers and optical and optoelectronic devices, reported in two segments. The Datacenter & Communications segment is the growth engine and the Industrial segment is shrinking through disposals. Ownership is public: no sponsor or controlling holder is named, although the sources do not list beneficial owners, and no dividend recapitalisation, priming or other creditor-adverse action is documented. The material events are the 2 billion NVIDIA share purchase, the conversion of the Series B preferred stock, the 2025 and 2026 disposals, the 2025 amendments to the Credit Agreement and the 2026 foreign credit facilities. The fact that most borrowing growth sits at foreign subsidiaries outside the guarantor group is a structural point for downstream work.

Three limits apply. First, ownership detail is incomplete: the annual report refers beneficial ownership to a proxy statement that is not in the pack, and the holder of the former Series B preferred stock is not named. Second, there is no transaction document, so use of proceeds is known only from filing summaries. Third, management statements about growth, margins and the AI opportunity are tagged Management Language and are not adopted. The governance view is a view of issuer-level behaviour from documented actions, not of individuals, and it is not a forecast of willingness under stress.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor transaction or new bond issue in the sources. The transactions that matter to a creditor are of four kinds. The first is the equity raise: on 2026-03-02 the company sold 7,788,161 shares to NVIDIA at 256.80 US dollars a share for aggregate gross proceeds of 2 billion US dollars, a private placement with a six-month lock-up and a six-month price protection provision that expired in September 2026 without being triggered. The company says the proceeds support research and development, capacity expansion and operations, and that a multi-year capacity agreement with NVIDIA may require incremental investment in equipment, labor and working capital through 2030 and may result in material future cash requirements. No amount is given for that agreement. This was equity, not debt. FY2026 cash flow shows share proceeds of 1,998,552 thousand while debt principal fell from 3,736,506 thousand to 3,257,482 thousand, but the sources do not say the proceeds were used to repay debt.

The second is the debt structure. On 2025-09-26 Amendments No. 4 and No. 5 to the Credit Agreement added 350 million of revolving commitments for a total of 700 million, added a 1,250 million Term A tranche to repay the existing Term A loans, and repriced the Term B loans; the revolver and Term A mature on 2030-09-26 unless a springing maturity applies. No new bond was issued; the 5.00% Senior Notes of 990 million date from 2021. The new borrowing is a set of unsecured facilities at foreign subsidiaries: the 2026 Credit Lines of up to 475 million, with 205 million outstanding at 2026-09-30, and the August 2026 Facility of about 950 million, with 598 million outstanding. These sit outside the guarantor group and are 802,793 thousand in total; the Company and its other subsidiaries are not parties to them. Their purpose includes funding working capital and repaying existing intercompany working capital loans, so the borrowing partly replaces internal funding with external debt at the subsidiary level.

The third is portfolio change. The aerospace and defense business was sold on 2025-09-02 for about 400 million with a 115 million gain, the Munich tools division was sold on 2026-01-30 at a stated loss of 96 million with a 9 million gain in the third quarter of FY2026, and a further entity classified as held for sale in the fourth quarter of FY2026 is expected to be sold within one year. The Q1 FY2027 note attributes a 115 million gain to the Munich sale, which conflicts with the annual report; the annual report and the quarterly statements are followed here. The fourth is the Silicon Carbide subsidiary: in December 2023 outside investors paid 1.0 billion for 25 percent of its equity, and the cash, 581 million of which remained at 2026-09-30, is restricted to that subsidiary. Use of proceeds, status and parties are Documentary Fact in each case; the executed agreements are not in the pack.

Other periods used: FY2025, Q1 FY2026 (three months ended 2025-09-30) and LTM (last twelve months to 2026-09-30).

Question for this module: what is the fundamental credit view, and which strengths, weaknesses, findings and risks drive it? The required decision drivers are business risk, financial risk and liquidity, and the gaps that limit both. Evidence is upstream only: this module reads no source text and quotes nothing. Every conclusion rests on the business and transaction fact rows of the context handoff (cited by their row ids F1 to F33 and T1 to T6) or on figures from the financial base handoff (cited by label and period), or on both. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Fundamentals are sound but stretched by growth: strong margins, 2.58x total and 1.46x net analyst leverage and 2,421.9 million of liquidity, against negative free cash flow, two large customers and unquantified commitments. | Medium | EBITDA and covenant ratios are analyst figures, and no customer terms, financing documents or sponsor detail are supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| LTM free cash flow was an outflow of 1,833,632 thousand, with Q1 FY2027 capital additions of 775,547 thousand. | Liquidity of 2,421.9 million covers about 2.8 quarters of the Q1 FY2027 cash burn, so the ramp must convert to EBITDA. | High |

| Datacenter & Communications was 82.3 percent of Q1 FY2027 revenue, and two customers were 20 percent and 12 percent of FY2026 revenue. | Revenue is concentrated, so a demand pause would cut EBITDA while debt and commitments stay fixed. | High |

| Foreign unsecured facilities of 802,793 thousand sit outside the guarantor group, and 95.8 percent of principal at 2026-06-30 falls due in FY2030 and FY2031. | Group creditors rank behind those lenders at the subsidiaries, and refinancing is concentrated in 2029 to 2031. | Medium |

| Analyst total debt to EBITDA fell from 4.43x in FY2025 to 2.29x in FY2026 and was 2.58x LTM, with 8.80x cover. | Leverage and cover are comfortable against the 4.25 to 1.00 and 2.50 to 1.00 covenants, but definitions are not supplied. | Medium |

| Governance actions are supportive: 502 million of voluntary repayment, preferred stock converted and no common dividends. | No creditor-adverse behaviour is documented, but legal capacity under the debt documents is not supplied. | Medium |
### Credit view

The fundamental credit view is of a company with strong and improving operating economics that is financing a very large capacity build, with the quality of that build to be proven. On the financial side, analyst EBITDA rose to 1,563,235 thousand LTM from 843,476 thousand in FY2025. Total debt to EBITDA fell from 4.43x in FY2025 to 2.29x in FY2026, and is 2.58x at 2026-09-30, with net debt to EBITDA of 1.46x. Cover is 8.80x on cash interest, and liquidity is 2,421.9 million made up of cash and short-term investments of 1,752.9 million and revolver availability of 669 million. The weight on the other side is cash flow. LTM free cash flow was an outflow of 1,833,632 thousand, Q1 FY2027 capital additions were 775,547 thousand, inventories and customer prepayments grew sharply, and the claims outside reported debt are large: purchase commitments of 3.4 billion for fiscal 2027 at 2026-06-30, contract liabilities, a capacity agreement that may need material cash, and operating leases.

On business risk, the company is a vertically integrated photonics manufacturer whose Datacenter & Communications segment was 74.1 percent of FY2026 revenue and 82.3 percent of Q1 FY2027 revenue, with two customers at 20 percent and 12 percent of FY2026 revenue and contract terms not supplied. Margins are expanding on yields, input costs and pricing, the equity base was strengthened by a 2 billion NVIDIA share purchase, and governance behaviour documented in the sources is supportive and not extractive. The structure of new debt is the point creditors should watch: most of the Q1 FY2027 increase of 775,916 thousand in principal is unsecured borrowing at foreign subsidiaries outside the guarantor group.

The overall view is therefore constructive on earnings and leverage, cautious on cash conversion, concentration and structure, and limited by missing documents. Confidence is Medium, not High: the readiness judgment for this module in the business handoff is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, covenant levels are not tied to a reported ratio, and no customer, ownership or legal-capacity evidence is supplied.
### Assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Strong and improving earnings and moderate analyst leverage, funding a heavy capacity build with negative free cash flow, concentrated revenue and rising claims outside debt | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | T1, T2, T3; CP-1 leverage, cover, liquidity and free cash flow for LTM and Q1 FY2027 |
### Thesis

Coherent can support its current debt because earnings and liquidity are strong, but the credit depends on converting a heavily funded capacity build and a concentrated AI datacenter demand base into EBITDA before cash and commitments tighten. Category: Analyst Interpretation. Basis: T1, T2, T6; CP-1 free cash flow and liquidity.
### Key findings

The first finding is cash conversion. In Q1 FY2027 operating cash flow was an outflow of 92,681 thousand and capital additions were 775,547 thousand, so free cash flow was an outflow of 868,228 thousand, and the LTM outflow was 1,833,632 thousand. The mechanism is the capacity and inventory build for AI demand: inventories rose by 760,330 thousand in the quarter, partly offset by accounts payable and customer prepayments, with accrued capital spending of 527,734 thousand in payables at 2026-09-30. The credit implication is that liquidity, not EBITDA, is the near-term constraint: 2,421.9 million of liquidity equals about 2.8 quarters of the Q1 FY2027 burn, and EBITDA less capital additions was negative for the LTM period. The company funded the gap with the 2 billion equity raise of March 2026, cash reserves (short-term investments fell from 825,000 thousand to 200,000 thousand) and 802,793 thousand of foreign borrowing. This is a Documentary Fact for the figures and an Analyst Interpretation for the reading (basis T2; F8, F10, F22).

The second is concentration. Datacenter & Communications was 82.3 percent of Q1 FY2027 revenue, North America was 65.1 percent of FY2026 revenue, and two customers were 20 percent and 12 percent of FY2026 revenue. Revenue visibility cannot be tested because customer contracts, volumes and pricing are not supplied, even though a multi-year supply agreement with NVIDIA is disclosed. The implication is that a pause by one large customer would reduce EBITDA quickly while debt service, leases and purchase commitments stay fixed. Basis: T1; F3, F7.

The third is structure. Unsecured borrowing at foreign subsidiaries of 802,793 thousand, which is 19.9 percent of principal, ranks ahead of group creditors at those subsidiaries, is not guaranteed by the Company or its other subsidiaries, and partly refinances intercompany loans. Foreign headroom is not group liquidity. Whether the debt documents cap such borrowing is not supplied. Basis: T3; F26, F27, F33.

The fourth is the covenant and maturity picture. Maintenance covenants of 4.25 to 1.00 net leverage and 2.50 to 1.00 interest cover apply to Term A and the revolver, and the company states compliance at 2026-09-30. On the analyst measure the cushions are about 65.7 percent and 71.6 percent of LTM EBITDA, but the credit agreement definitions are not supplied, so these are indicative only. At 2026-06-30, 95.8 percent of principal falls in FY2030 and FY2031, with the Term B on 2029-07-01 and the notes on 2029-12-15; the revolver and Term A can spring to 91 days before those dates if the notes or Term B are outstanding and liquidity is below the stated test. Basis: CP-1 covenant and maturity data.

The fifth is governance and external exposure. The documented record is supportive: 502 million of voluntary term loan repayment in FY2026, preferred stock converted and its dividends waived, and no common dividends. Against that, most of the workforce is in Asia-Pacific, China was 11.4 percent of FY2026 revenue, and an export-control inquiry about past sales to Huawei has no loss estimate. Basis: T4, T5; F5, F11 to F15, F24, F25.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strengths are as follows. First, scale and operating leverage: FY2026 revenue was 7,118,181 thousand, up 22.5 percent, Q1 FY2027 revenue was up 49.9 percent, and Q1 FY2027 gross margin rose 254 basis points on yields, input costs and pricing, to 39.1 percent, so EBITDA is growing faster than debt (basis F21; CP-1 revenue and margin). Second, moderate leverage and strong cover: total debt to EBITDA of 2.58x, net debt to EBITDA of 1.46x and EBITDA to cash interest of 8.80x LTM, though on an analyst EBITDA that includes 8,922 thousand of gain (CP-1 leverage and cover data). Third, liquidity and a distant maturity wall: 2,421.9 million of liquidity, an undrawn revolver, and only 7.916, 34.375 and 93.629 million due in FY2027 to FY2029 as of 2026-06-30. Fourth, supportive governance in documented actions and a 2 billion equity infusion with no debt service (T5; F8, F13, F15). Fifth, vertical integration and a disclosed multi-year supply agreement with a major AI customer (F1, F7); the claim of a leading supplier position is Management Language and is not adopted (F6).

The weaknesses are as follows. First, concentration in one end market and two customers (T1; F3). Second, negative free cash flow and capital intensity, with capital additions of 32.7 percent of Q1 FY2027 revenue (T2; F22). Third, structural subordination from foreign unsecured debt (T3). Fourth, claims outside reported debt that raise cash demands: purchase commitments of 3.4 billion for fiscal 2027 and 8.4 billion thereafter at 2026-06-30, contract liabilities of 333 million, operating lease liabilities of 346,382 thousand, and a capacity agreement with no stated amount (F10; CP-1 claims outside debt). Fifth, refinancing concentration in 2029 to 2031 and about 75.0 percent of principal at variable rates, where the effect of hedges is not in the upstream handoffs. Sixth, operational and trade exposure in Asia-Pacific with an unquantified export inquiry (T4). Seventh, limited visibility: no reported EBITDA, covenant ratio, customer terms or executed financing documents, and three logged conflicts in the latest quarterly report (F32, F33; C1 to C3).

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: COHERENT CORP. (cohr; NYSE COHR). As-of date: 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency USD; the statements are in thousands of US dollars, the narrative and liquidity tables in millions. Periods: FY2025 and FY2026 (years ended 30 June), Q1 FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 (three months ended 2025-09-30 and 2026-09-30) and LTM (last twelve months to 2026-09-30).

Question: does each material claim in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis handoffs rest on the evidence it names, and do the three tell one consistent story? The review traces claims to the pinned filings and releases, re-computes derived figures, compares figures and scope across the handoffs, grades the set and states whether committee use is permitted, restricted or blocked. The source readiness handoff is the gate and is graded only for the claims that later handoffs rely on. The review changes no figure in another handoff; where it disagrees it says so here, because an accepted handoff cannot be edited.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Figures and quotes in the handoffs trace to the filings and recompute exactly, and the handoffs agree with each other. Committee use is restricted because covenant definitions, customer terms and executed debt documents are missing, not because tracing failed. | Medium | The review was run in the same session as the analysis, from the same extraction text, so it is not an independent second review. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| All 36 quoted spans in the business handoff and all 31 in the readiness handoff were found in the sources, and every derived figure in the financial handoff recomputed exactly. | The numbers and wording a committee would quote can be relied on as labelled. | High |

| Three statements are only partly supported: the 803 million of new borrowing, equity proceeds as the cause of lower debt, and the purpose of the 2026 Credit Lines. | These are wording and attribution points; the underlying figures are right and the credit direction is unaffected. | Medium |

| Two locator or label points were found in the readiness handoff: one page reference for the August 2026 facility, and a stray header line read as a label slip. | Minor precision issues that change no figure. | High |

| No contradiction between the handoffs was found, and the three logged source conflicts remain open. | The set tells one consistent story, but disclosure errors in the latest quarterly report stay unreconciled. | Medium |

| Covenant ratios, customer terms, the capacity agreement amount and executed debt documents are not in the sources. | Headroom, concentration and legal capacity cannot be tested, so committee use is restricted. | High |
### Evidence trace view

The evidence trace holds. Each material claim in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis handoffs was matched to a located source span or to a recomputation from located figures, and the three handoffs agree on every shared figure, period and perimeter label. The cautious credit view of the synthesis, with Medium confidence, follows from its cited basis and is not overstated. Three claims are only partly supported, all as wording or attribution rather than figures: the description of 803 million as new borrowing in the quarter, the reading that the equity raise funded the free cash flow gap or the fall in debt, and the statement that both groups of foreign facilities repay intercompany loans. One locator and one label point were found in the readiness handoff. No claim is unsupported and no module contradicts another. The integrity verdict for the evaluated set is nonetheless Restricted, not Committee Ready, because the conclusions that matter most to a creditor, namely covenant headroom, concentration in two customers, the size of the NVIDIA capacity agreement and the legal capacity to add debt, rest on documents that are not in the sources. The review itself is limited: it was done in the same session as the analysis, from the same extraction text, and the page locators are extraction chunks rather than printed pages.

### Cross-module contradictions

None found. Pairs examined and found consistent: falling analyst leverage in CP-1 against rising debt in Q1 FY2027 (CP-1 and CP-2 both say the principal rose while the LTM EBITDA rose faster); strong cover in CP-1 against negative free cash flow in CP-2; a distant maturity wall in CP-1 against the springing maturity test in CP-2; the supportive governance reading in CP-1A against the 802,793 of foreign debt outside the guarantor group in CP-2 (CP-1A tags that point Neutral or Mixed, and CP-2 lists it as a risk); and management's growth claims in CP-1A (tagged Management Language, not adopted) against the cautious view in CP-2.
### Verdict consistency

The verdicts agree across modules for every shared claim. The confidence of Medium in CP-2 is no higher than the readiness judgment of ready with limitations in CP-1A allows, and its listed gaps match the inherited gaps. The integrity grade of the set is Restricted with Medium confidence.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the cautious reading is that the earnings base is growing fast: analyst EBITDA rose from 843,476 in FY2025 to 1,563,235 on an LTM basis, Q1 FY2027 EBITDA to cash interest was 17.86x, liquidity of 2,421.9 million is above the springing tests, and management states fiscal 2027 growth well above fiscal 2026. If capital additions of 775,547 in Q1 FY2027 are mainly the capacity build that peaks and then converts to EBITDA, free cash flow would recover quickly. What would make that case win: Q2 FY2027 revenue inside the guided 2.55 billion to 2.75 billion range, a lower Q2 capital additions figure than in Q1, and falling inventory growth. Downside chain with observable triggers: a pause in orders from one of the two large customers (first break: revenue and gross margin) lowers EBITDA while capital commitments of 3.4 billion for fiscal 2027 and lease and debt service stay fixed (transmission), then liquidity falls below 2,421.9 million and revolver availability below 669 million (consequence), then the springing test of 250 million plus the Term B or notes principal becomes relevant before 2029 and refinancing of the 2029 to 2031 wall is harder. Triggers to watch: customer order trends, capital additions, inventory and contract liabilities each quarter, revolver availability, and the covenant certificate when obtainable.

## Next module

None remains in the selected set. The integrity verdict is Committee use restricted: the research may support a screening view of earnings direction, liquidity, the maturity profile, debt structure and business risk with its stated labels, but should not support covenant headroom, legal capacity, customer concentration terms or recovery conclusions until the gaps above are closed. Next actions in order: obtain the executed Credit Agreement, amendments and Indenture; obtain the compliance certificate or covenant definitions; obtain customer and capacity agreement disclosure; have a second reviewer compare the handoffs with the original filings before external use.
